episodes.178523: A cluster of severe thunderstorms moved across the area and produced hail, damaging winds and flash flooding.
episodes.178538: A weak cold front passed through, with around 1500 to 2000 J/kg of SBCAPE ahead of it. Deep layer shear was 30 to 40 kts. An isolated supercell developed in western Wisconsin and produced 1 to 1.75 inch hail in Pierce County. There was also a tornado warning issued, but no reports of damage or a funnel.
episodes.178586: A severe thunderstorm developed on the northeast side of Rapid City and tracked east-northeast across portions of the west central South Dakota plains. The storm produced hail to golf ball size along its path.
episodes.178588: A severe thunderstorm developed over the Belle Fourche area and tracked east across far southern Butte County, producing hail to at least quarter size.
episodes.178685: Isolated thunderstorms across far northern central Indiana included one rotating supercell whose persistent nature contributed to a landspout tornado spawning.  The tornado was displaced to the south of the cell's mesocyclone, which is atypical for supercell tornadoes.
episodes.178763: Thunderstorms developed in the afternoon of May 8th across southwestern Puerto Rico. As the evening progressed, the thunderstorms redeveloped over the western coastal waters of the islands, and a waterspout developed of one storm.
episodes.178868: Two mesoscale convective systems produced large hail and damaging winds across East Tennessee.
episodes.179004: A broken line of showers and thunderstorms moved eastward across southwest Indiana. The storms were associated with a warm front that extended from Missouri eastward to the middle Ohio Valley. A lightning strike resulted in one injury.
episodes.179258: Convection began in early afternoon in eastern Iowa along a subtle boundary across the state. This was fueled by high CAPE exceeding 3000 J/kg with deep layer shear sufficient to support large hail growth. Later in the evening a secondary round of convection moved across the area producing additional hail in the form of a cold pool driven MCS, driven along the plume of higher instability. The result was dozen of hail reports up to baseball sized across much of central and southern Iowa, damaging homes and vehicles and taking down power lines. As storms crossed Interstate 80 an accident resulted in significant delays.
episodes.179299: Storms developed over the central Plains near the Kansas and Nebraska border during the afternoon of the 7th and moved southeastward across central and south central Missouri from the pre-dawn hours to the early morning of the 8th. These storms left an outflow boundary over central Missouri that sparked a second round of storms during the afternoon. These storms were much stronger and produced hail across central Missouri through the evening of the  8th. The strongest storm produced hail to the size of baseballs in Dent County near Stone Hill. Rainfall amounts over two inches occurred with these storms near Nevada, Lake of the Ozarks, and north of Salem.
episodes.179478: On the afternoon of May 6 strong thunderstorms formed in far northwest Missouri. Through the afternoon these storms strengthened as they moved east across northern Missouri, ultimately turning into robust supercells that started diving southeast toward Highway 36. Along the way they produced giant hail reaching, and perhaps exceeding 4 inches at times. As the main storm pushed southeast toward Linneus, Missouri it produced a tornado that at times was several hundred yards wide. This tornado produced EF-2 damage just north of Linneus. Perhaps as noteworthy, if not more so, was the extremely strong and wide rear flank downdraft that produced some intense damage well south of the main tornado track. This RFD destroyed numerous homes along the way and produced extreme tree damage to the city of Linneus, which was largely spared a direct hit from the actual tornado. Overall the storm produced three separate tornadoes, the most noteworthy of which was the EF-2 just north of Linneus, Missouri.
episodes.179800: An outflow boundary from convection that occurred during the early morning served as the focusing mechanism for additional severe thunderstorm development during the afternoon and evening of May 7th.  The storms initially focused along a Macomb...to Springfield...to Mount Vernon line and were very slow-moving in nature.  Due to a feed of highly unstable air characterized by CAPE values in excess of 3000J/kg, vigorous updrafts quickly developed and supported giant hail.  Hailstones as large as 3.25 inches in diameter were reported in the town of Chatham in Sangamon County, causing significant damage to homes and vehicles.  Numerous other thunderstorm cells produced hail larger than quarters, with the slow-movement of the cells causing some locations to report hail lasting for greater than 30 minutes.  As storms merged into a large cluster, the severe weather threat temporarily waned: however, flash flooding developed across southern portions of Sangamon and Christian counties as rainfall amounts of 4 to 6 inches were common across this area.  By early evening, a line of thunderstorms developed further north along a cold front across eastern Iowa into northern Illinois.  As the line sagged southward, damaging wind gusts of 60 to 70mph produced scattered wind damage along and north of a Canton to Bloomington line.
episodes.179955: Middle to upper level winds were out of the west to southwest, and an upper level disturbance moved over the region from Colorado by the early evening hours. There was a weak surface low to the south with an inverted trough axis over portions of north central Kansas and south central Nebraska extending north of the low. This trough axis set up a frontal zone across Nebraska and Kansas. High based thunderstorms developed to the west of the area along a shortwave trough then moved eastward and encountered increased instability. Mixed layer CAPE was around 1000 to 2000 J/kg and deep layer wind shear was around 50 to 60 knots. There was a slight risk of severe storms from the Storm Prediction Center. ||Storms began developing to the west and northwest of the area during the afternoon hours. A cluster of storms moved in from the west and began impacting north central Kansas around 7 pm. This cluster of storms continued moving eastward during the evening hours and extended northward into portions of southern Nebraska. The cluster exited the area around 10:30 pm as it continued tracking eastward across Nebraska. There were several strong to severe wind gusts across north central Kansas and one report of golfball sized hail. One report of thunderstorm wind damage occurred in Mitchell County. The storms went on to produce a few severe wind gusts in Nuckolls and Thayer Counties in Nebraska as well as a wind damage report in Thayer County.

episodes.180049: An Enhanced Risk was issued for severe weather on May 7. A shortwave moving across the area interacted with a couple of surface boundaries in the area initiating severe weather. There were numerous hail and wind reports across the area. The largest hail report was 2.5 inches in Lancaster County and the highest measured wind gust was 73 mph in Richardson County.
episodes.180073: A weak mesoscale convective vortex (MCV), leftover from showers and thunderstorms that developed during the afternoon and evening across North Texas on May 7th, drifted east into Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and Northwest Louisiana during the late morning and afternoon hours on May 8th. This disturbance interacted with a moist and moderately unstable air mass in place during the period of peak heating and generated adequate forcing for the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms across the region. Some of these storms became severe across extreme Southeast Oklahoma, East Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and Northwest Louisiana, producing large hail and damaging winds before weakening during the evening with the loss of heating and reduced instability.
episodes.180075: A weak mesoscale convective vortex (MCV), leftover from showers and thunderstorms that developed during the afternoon and evening across North Texas on May 7th, drifted east into Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and Northwest Louisiana during the late morning and afternoon hours on May 8th. This disturbance interacted with a moist and moderately unstable air mass in place during the period of peak heating and generated adequate forcing for the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms across the region. Some of these storms became severe across extreme Southeast Oklahoma, East Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and Northwest Louisiana, producing large hail and damaging winds before weakening during the evening with the loss of heating and reduced instability.
episodes.180080: An Enhanced Risk was issued for severe weather on May 7. A shortwave moving across the area interacted with a couple of surface boundaries in the area initiating severe weather. There was video of a weak tornado that didn't produce any damage. There were several hail reports the largest of which was 2.25 inches in Mills County.
episodes.180205: A storm system moved through Utah, resulting in sporadic incidences of strong winds.
episodes.180262: The tail end of large scale forcing associated with an upper-level low moving across North Dakota brushed through far eastern South Dakota, southwest Minnesota, and northwest Iowa just after diurnal heating maximum. With a weak moisture convergence axis and 500-1000 J/kg MLCAPE in the presence of 40 knots of deep-layer shear, isolated multicell storms developed which produced marginally large hail during the very brief life cycle.

episodes.180485: Heavy showers developed over the Portland metro area in the afternoon as a cool upper trough remained over the region. Minor flooding occurred in the area. The greatest impacts were to a southwest Portland neighborhood where 14 homes were affected.
episodes.180489: Several severe thunderstorms developed across much of eastern Iowa on the evening of May 6, 2023. Storms mainly produced hail up to golf ball size. Through the evening, storms merged and weakened in intensity, but not before producing some wind damage across northern and central Lee County. An isolated tornado also occurred in Muscatine County. Heavy rain also fell from storms as some remained stationary for long periods of time. Most notably, locations north and east of Fairfield, Iowa recorded over two inches of rain.
episodes.180495: Several rounds of severe thunderstorms impacted the area on Sunday May 7, 2023.  Two areas of storms were present during the mid to late afternoon, one entering the Cedar Rapids and Iowa City metros and another around the Burlington and Fort Madison metros. The first was the most severe, producing hail up to baseball size in Koszta, Iowa and widespread wind damage, especially around West Liberty, Iowa. This storm, and storms to the west, eventually merged into a cluster of severe thunderstorms, producing large hail and destructive winds around 70-75 mph all the way to Mount Pleasant, Iowa and Macomb, Illinois. The latter produced sporadic reports of quarter to half dollar sized hail, along with a brief landspout tornado east of Yorktown, IL.  There was also severe blowing dust which was especially bad near I-55 in north central Illinois. Even more thunderstorms developed overnight across the area, and mainly produced torrential rain and isolated large hail reports.
episodes.180496: Several rounds of severe thunderstorms impacted the area on Sunday May 7, 2023.  Two areas of storms were present during the mid to late afternoon, one entering the Cedar Rapids and Iowa City metros and another around the Burlington and Fort Madison metros. The first was the most severe, producing hail up to baseball size in Koszta, Iowa and widespread wind damage, especially around West Liberty, Iowa. This storm, and storms to the west, eventually merged into a cluster of severe thunderstorms, producing large hail and destructive winds around 70-75 mph all the way to Mount Pleasant, Iowa and Macomb, Illinois. The latter produced sporadic reports of quarter to half dollar sized hail, along with a brief landspout tornado east of Yorktown, IL.  There was also severe blowing dust which was especially bad near I-55 in north central Illinois. Even more thunderstorms developed overnight across the area, and mainly produced torrential rain and isolated large hail reports.
episodes.180540: The combination of a well defined surface dryline, weak upper level disturbances, and strong to extreme instability, resulted in scattered afternoon and evening severe thunderstorms across portions of the Big Country and Concho Valley. The severe storms were mainly north and east of a Rotan to Abilene to San Angelo to Cross Plains line. The vertical wind shear was strong enough for most of the storms to become supercell thunderstorms. The severe storms produced mainly large to very large hail.
episodes.180658: A line of thunderstorms produced severe weather, mainly across northern Kansas during the evening of 5/7.
episodes.180753: On the evening of May 7th, a line of thunderstorms produced severe winds, severe hail, heavy rain, and even two landspouts across parts of the southern and southwestern Chicago metro. The heaviest of the rainfall occurred along a narrow corridor stretching from far southern Lee County southeastward into east-central Kankakee County where widespread 2+ inch rainfall totals were reported with a few spots seeing between four and five inches of rain. Additionally, strong outflow winds from nearby thunderstorms kicked up significant amounts of blowing dust across parts of southern LaSalle County and towards the I-55 corridor in Livingston County. This was preceded by an abnormally dry period stretching back to early April leading to dry soil conditions in the area. Multiple reports of near-zero visibility resulted in the issuance of two Dust Storm Warnings, the first such warnings issued by the Chicago WFO.
episodes.180754: On the evening of May 7th, a line of thunderstorms produced heavy rain, strong winds, and severe hail across portions of northwest Indiana. Swaths of 1.5 to 2.5 inches of rain fell across parts of Newton, Jasper, and Benton Counties as well as extreme southwestern Lake County.
episodes.180871: Thunderstorms developed in a weakly capped, conditionally unstable airmass along an old outflow boundary. Some of these storms produced large hail and localized flash flooding.
episodes.181049: Upper disturbances moved across the region and interacted with a very moist air mass to produce scattered to numerous thunderstorms. Some storms became severe.
episodes.181081: A weakening upper ridge combined with weak warm advection and a moderately unstable airmass resulted in scattered thunderstorms across northeast Mississippi during the evening hours of May 7, 2023. A storm over Lee County became severe with large hail.
episodes.181112: As an MCV moved through southeastern MO, it combined with an old outflow boundary. They were the focusing mechanism for storm development. Severe storms developed over portions of southwestern, south central and west central Illinois. There were a number of reports of very large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.181129: A subtle/low-amplitude trough helped to trigger scattered strong to severe storms across western-north Texas/far southwest Oklahoma on the 7th. A few reports of damaging wind and large hail were noted. Repeated rounds of heavy rainfall across portions of Knox County, Texas lead to reports of flash flooding.
episodes.181239: An upper level trough moved southeast through the region, triggering showers and storms. Some of the storms became severe and produced damaging winds.
episodes.181240: A strong cold front moved south through the region with plenty of instability, high mid-level lapse rates and strong 0 to 6km bulk shear. Given this environment, a number of storms became severe with widespread reports of large hail, some in excess of 2 inches in diameter.
episodes.181241: On the evening/night of May 7th, a squall line moved from NW Missouri into central MO, leading to a couple of wind reports.
episodes.181242: In the late afternoon of May 8th, severe storms dropped half dollar and ping pong ball hail in Bates County.
episodes.181243: A storm produced half dollar hail in Linn County, KS on the late afternoon of May 8th.
episodes.181393: A broken line of heavy rain showers and thunderstorms developed across western North Carolina during the late afternoon and evening and moved southeast into upstate South Carolina by mid-evening. One severe thunderstorm produced a swath of wind damage in Spartanburg County.
episodes.181421: A slow moving storm brought heavy rains to the area. Rain and snow melt led to a debris flow near the 25 Mile Creek Burn Scar.
